Note the difference: এক কাপ uses the bare number before a measure word; একটা is used when you count the things themselves.

কম (kom) is 'less' and বেশি (beshi) 'more': চিনি কম, 'less sugar'. 'Without' is ছাড়া (chhaaraa) after the noun: চিনি ছাড়া চা, 'tea without sugar'.

To refuse more food, say ব্যস (byas) 'enough' or আর লাগবে না, 'no more needed'. A good host will insist; refusing twice is normal.

examples.english: No sugar in the tea, please.

guide.title: Hungry, thirsty, full
guide.text:
You are not hungry in Bengali; hunger 'gets' you. The person is in the possessive: আমার খিদে পেয়েছে, 'my hunger has got' - I am hungry. In the same way আমার তেষ্টা পেয়েছে (aamaar teshtaa peyechhe), 'I am thirsty'.

When you have had enough: আমার পেট ভরে গেছে, 'my stomach has filled up'.

To praise the food, say it 'has turned out' well: খাবারটা খুব ভালো হয়েছে; or simply দারুণ! (daarun) 'terrific!'

আপনি খেয়েছেন? - 'Have you eaten?' - is asked out of friendliness at any time around a mealtime. It is a greeting as much as a question.

phrases.note: Literally 'hunger has got me'.
In Bangladesh water is 'paani' (পানি).
The first-person present works as 'let me ...'.
Literally 'I eat vegetarian food'.

phrases.english: No sugar in the tea, please.
That's enough, I don't want any more.

phrases.note: Literally 'the food has turned out very well'.
A common friendly question, almost a greeting.
The ending -taa works like 'the'.

units.title: Directions & getting around
units.description: Ask where a place is, follow and give directions, and deal with taxis, rickshaws and buses.

guide.title: Where is it?
guide.text:
'Where is X?' is X + কোথায়? with no verb: স্টেশনটা কোথায়? The -টা shows you mean a particular one - the station, the toilet, the hospital.

To ask the way: X কোন দিকে? (kon dike) 'which way is X?'; X কীভাবে যাব? (keebhaabe jaabo) 'how do I get to X?'

Distance: কত দূর? (koto door) 'how far?'; কাছে (kaachhe) near; কাছেই (kaachhei) 'quite near, just here'; দূরে (doore) far; পাঁচ মিনিটের রাস্তা 'a five-minute walk'.

The little -ই (-i) on কাছেই is the emphatic particle: 'right nearby'.

examples.english: How far is it from here?

guide.title: Left, right, straight
guide.text:
ডান দিকে (daan dike) to the right
বাঁ দিকে (baan dike) to the left - written form বাম দিকে (baam dike)
সোজা (shojaa) straight on
সামনে (shaamne) ahead, in front
পেছনে (pechhone) behind, back
মোড় (mor) a crossing, a street corner
পাশে (paashe) beside; উল্টো দিকে (ulto dike) opposite, on the other side

The polite commands: যান (jaan) go; চলুন (cholun) go on, let's go; ঘুরুন (ghurun) turn; থামুন (thaamun) stop; দাঁড়ান (daanraan) stop and wait; নামুন (naamun) get down.

দিক (dik) is 'direction, side'; with the 'at' ending it becomes দিকে.

guide.title: Taxis, rickshaws, buses
guide.text:
To a taxi or rickshaw driver, first ask whether he will go: হাওড়া স্টেশন যাবেন? 'Will you go to Howrah station?' Then agree the fare: কত ভাড়া? or কত নেবেন? 'How much will you take?' ভাড়া (bhaaraa) is a fare or a rent.

To say where you want to go, use the plain future: আমি এয়ারপোর্টে যাব, 'I will go to the airport'.

By a means of transport takes the 'at' ending: বাসে, ট্রেনে, ট্যাক্সিতে, রিকশায় (rikshaay), মেট্রোয় (metroy). On foot is হেঁটে (hente), 'walking'.

Getting on is ওঠা (othaa) and getting off is নামা (naamaa): এখানে নামব, 'I'll get off here'.

On a bus, ask the conductor: এই বাসটা কি ... যাবে?

examples.english: Will you go to Howrah station?
I want to go to the airport.

phrases.note: 'baathrum' is the everyday polite word for toilet.

phrases.english: How far is it from here?

phrases.note: Short 'ki' (কি) marks a yes/no question; long 'kee' (কী) means 'what'.
বাঁ has a nasal vowel. The written form is বাম (baam).
To a taxi or rickshaw driver you can also say 'ekhaane daanraan' (এখানে দাঁড়ান).

phrases.english: Will you go to Howrah station?
phrases.note: How to hail a taxi or rickshaw: ask whether the driver will go there.

phrases.english: I want to go to the airport.
phrases.note: Literally 'I will go to the airport'. The Bengali word is বিমানবন্দর (bimaanbondor).

phrases.native: এই বাসটা কি পার্ক স্ট্রিট যাবে?
phrases.roman: ei baastaa ki paark strit jaabe?
phrases.english: Does this bus go to Park Street?
I'll get off at the corner.

units.title: Shopping, money and numbers to 100
units.description: Ask prices, understand the answer, bargain and pay, using the numbers from eleven to a hundred.

guide.title: Eleven to sixteen
guide.text:
Bengali numbers up to a hundred are not built by a simple rule like 'twenty-one, twenty-two': each one is a single word that has to be learnt. The good news is that the pattern is visible once you know the units and the tens, and that everyone understands you if you say the digits one by one.

The numbers from eleven to eighteen all end in a spoken -o, now usually written with ো.

guide.title: Seventeen to thirty
guide.text:
Nineteen is 'one less than twenty': উনিশ. The same উন- prefix gives 29 (উনত্রিশ), 39 (উনচল্লিশ) and so on.

Twenty is কুড়ি (kuri) in West Bengal and বিশ (bish) in Bangladesh; both are understood everywhere. The twenties are built on the older form: একুশ (ekush) 21, বাইশ (baaish) 22, তেইশ (teish) 23, চব্বিশ (chobbish) 24, পঁচিশ (ponchish) 25.

Thirty is তিরিশ in everyday speech, ত্রিশ (trish) in writing.

guide.title: The tens
guide.text:
With the tens you can understand most prices, because shopkeepers round to five or ten.

ষাট (sixty) and সাত (seven) are both romanised shaat: sixty has the retroflex t (tongue curled back), seven the dental t (tongue on the teeth).

A hundred is একশো (eksho), also written একশ. Then দুশো (dusho) 200, তিনশো 300, পাঁচশো 500; হাজার (haajaar) 1,000; লাখ (laakh) 100,000.

guide.title: Hundreds, and the 'half' words
guide.text:
The currency is the টাকা (taakaa): the rupee in India, the taka in Bangladesh. The word also simply means 'money'. The amount comes first: পঞ্চাশ টাকা, 'fifty rupees'.

Bengali has special words for one and a half and two and a half, and they are used all the time with money, weights and clock times:

দেড় (der) one and a half - দেড়শো 150, দেড় কিলো 1.5 kg
আড়াই (aaraai) two and a half - আড়াইশো 250
সাড়ে (shaare) 'plus a half', from three and a half upwards - সাড়ে তিনশো 350, সাড়ে পাঁচ কিলো 5.5 kg

Never say সাড়ে এক or সাড়ে দুই.

guide.title: Asking the price and bargaining
guide.text:
দাম (daam) is 'price'. এটার দাম কত? 'What is the price of this?' - or just point and say কত? For things sold by weight: কত করে? (koto kore) 'how much each / per kilo?'

In markets and small shops without fixed prices, bargaining is expected and good-humoured. The standard moves: এত দাম! 'so much!'; একটু কম করুন, 'reduce it a little'; then name your figure with দেব, 'I'll give': দেড়শো টাকা দেব।

To close: ঠিক আছে, দিন - 'all right, give it to me'. To walk away politely: আমার লাগবে না - 'I won't need it'. To look without pressure: আমি শুধু দেখছি।

খুচরো (khuchro) is small change; ফেরত (pherot) is the change you get back.

examples.english: Please reduce the price a little.
I'll give a hundred and fifty rupees.

phrases.note: টাকা is the rupee in India and the taka in Bangladesh.
Literally 'the price is very high'.

phrases.english: Please reduce the price a little.
phrases.note: The standard bargaining phrase.
In Bangladesh twenty is বিশ (bish).

phrases.english: I'll give a hundred and fifty rupees.
phrases.note: দেড় is 'one and a half'.
Literally 'I won't need it' - a polite way to refuse.

phrases.english: Do you have a bigger size?

phrases.note: You will hear this from shopkeepers too.

units.title: Family
units.description: Introduce your family, ask about someone else's, and find your way through the Bengali words for relatives.

guide.title: The immediate family
guide.text:
মা (maa) mother; বাবা (baabaa) father; বাবা-মা or মা-বাবা parents.
ছেলে (chhele) son, boy; মেয়ে (meye) daughter, girl; ছেলেমেয়ে children.
স্বামী (shaamee) husband; স্ত্রী (stree) wife. The homely words are বর (bor) and বউ (bou).

Brothers and sisters are divided by age. ভাই and বোন are the general words for 'brother' and 'sister', but an elder brother or sister is always called দাদা or দিদি, so ভাই and বোন on their own are normally understood as younger ones.

দাদা (daadaa) elder brother - দিদি (didi) elder sister
ভাই (bhaai) younger brother - বোন (bon) younger sister
ভাইবোন (bhaaibon) brothers and sisters, siblings

Elder brothers and sisters are addressed as দাদা and দিদি, never by name alone; younger ones are called by name.

examples.english: We are three brothers and sisters.

guide.title: Father's side and mother's side
guide.text:
Uncles, aunts and grandparents have different names on the father's and the mother's side. These are the words used in West Bengal and by Bengali Hindus generally.

Father's side: ঠাকুরদা (thaakurdaa) grandfather; ঠাকুমা (thaakumaa) grandmother; জ্যাঠা (jyaathaa) father's elder brother; কাকা (kaakaa) father's younger brother; পিসি (pishi) father's sister.

Mother's side: দাদু (daadu) grandfather; দিদা (didaa) grandmother; মামা (maamaa) mother's brother; মাসি (maashi) mother's sister.

Many families use দাদু for both grandfathers.

Cousins are called brothers and sisters, with an adjective if you need to be exact: মামাতো ভাই (maamaato bhaai) 'son of my mother's brother', মাসতুতো বোন (maashtuto bon) 'daughter of my mother's sister'.

examples.english: My grandfather lives in the village.
He is my uncle (father's younger brother).

guide.title: The words used in Bangladesh
guide.text:
Bengali Muslims, and so most people in Bangladesh, use a partly different set, much of it from Persian and Arabic.

আব্বা (aabbaa) or আব্বু father; আম্মা (aammaa) or আম্মু mother
ভাইয়া (bhaaiyaa) or বড় ভাই elder brother; আপা (aapaa) or আপু elder sister
দাদা (daadaa) father's father; দাদি (daadi) father's mother
নানা (naanaa) mother's father; নানি (naani) mother's mother
চাচা (chaachaa) father's brother; ফুফু (phuphu) father's sister
মামা (maamaa) mother's brother; খালা (khaalaa) mother's sister

The trap is দাদা: in West Bengal it is an elder brother, in Bangladesh a paternal grandfather.

examples.english: She is my elder sister (Bangladesh usage).
My maternal grandfather lives in Dhaka.

guide.title: Respect inside the family
guide.text:
When you talk ABOUT an older relative, use the respectful verb ending -en: বাবা অফিসে আছেন; দাদু গ্রামে থাকেন. For a younger brother, a child or a friend, use the ordinary -e: আমার মেয়ে স্কুলে পড়ে।

When you talk TO them, most people today call their parents and elder brothers and sisters তুমি; আপনি to one's own parents is old-fashioned, though still heard. In-laws and other people's parents are আপনি.

To ask whether someone is married, Bengali says 'has your marriage happened?': আপনার কি বিয়ে হয়েছে? বিয়ে (biye) is 'wedding, marriage'.

Asking after the family is basic politeness: বাড়ির সবাই কেমন আছেন? - 'How is everyone at home?'

phrases.note: স before ত is a true s: stree.
The ব under স is silent.
'daadaa' is elder brother in West Bengal; a younger brother is 'bhaai' (ভাই). In Bangladesh দাদা is a paternal grandfather.
An elder sister is 'didi' (দিদি).

phrases.english: We are three brothers and sisters.

phrases.note: A question strangers ask quite freely.

phrases.english: How many people are there in your family?
My grandfather lives in the village.
phrases.note: 'daadu' is used for either grandfather; a paternal grandfather is also 'thaakurdaa' (ঠাকুরদা).
Specifically the son of a mother's brother.

units.title: Time, days and dates
units.description: Tell the time, name the days of the week and the parts of the day, and talk about today, tomorrow and yesterday.

guide.title: What time is it?
guide.text:
The hour is the number with the counting ending -টা: একটা (ektaa) one o'clock, দুটো (duto), তিনটে (tinte), চারটে (chaarte), পাঁচটা (paanchtaa), ছটা (chhotaa), সাতটা (shaattaa), আটটা (aattaa), নটা (notaa), দশটা (doshtaa), এগারোটা (egaarotaa), বারোটা (baarotaa).

কটা বাজে? is 'how many is it striking?' - What time is it? The answer: পাঁচটা বাজে, 'it is striking five', or just এখন পাঁচটা।

Half past uses সাড়ে (shaare) before the hour: সাড়ে পাঁচটা, 5:30. But 1:30 is দেড়টা (dertaa) and 2:30 is আড়াইটে (aaraaite).

Quarter past is সওয়া (showaa): সওয়া পাঁচটা, 5:15. Quarter to is পৌনে (poune): পৌনে ছটা, 5:45.

Other minutes: পাঁচটা দশ, 5:10; ছটা বাজতে দশ, 'ten to six'.

'At' a time is the ending -য় (-y): পাঁচটায় (paanchtaay) at five; দুটোয় (dutoy) at two; তিনটেয় (tintey) at three; কটায়? (kotaay) at what time?

examples.english: It is half past one now.
Please come at half past seven.

guide.title: Parts of the day
guide.text:
Bengali does not use a.m. and p.m. in speech; the part of the day is named before the hour.

ভোর (bhor) dawn, early morning
সকাল (shokaal) morning
দুপুর (dupur) midday, early afternoon
বিকেল (bikel) late afternoon
সন্ধে (shondhe) evening, dusk - written form সন্ধ্যা (shondhaa)
রাত (raat) night

সকাল আটটা, 8 a.m.; রাত আটটা, 8 p.m.; দুপুর দুটো, 2 p.m.; ভোর পাঁচটা, 5 a.m.

'In the morning' takes the 'at' ending or the word বেলা (belaa) 'time of day': সকালে or সকালবেলা; বিকেলে; সন্ধেবেলা; রাতে.

guide.title: Days of the week
guide.text:
Each day name ends in বার (baar) 'day of the week':

রবিবার (robibaar) Sunday
সোমবার (shombaar) Monday
মঙ্গলবার (mongolbaar) Tuesday
বুধবার (budhbaar) Wednesday
বৃহস্পতিবার (brihoshpotibaar) Thursday
শুক্রবার (shukrobaar) Friday
শনিবার (shonibaar) Saturday

'On Monday' is just সোমবার or সোমবারে. 'What day is it?' is আজ কী বার? 'What is the date?' is আজ কত তারিখ? - dates, being numbers, are asked with কত.

সপ্তাহ (shoptaaho) week; মাস (maash) month; বছর (bochhor) year; দিন (din) day; ঘণ্টা (ghontaa) hour.

examples.english: The day after tomorrow is Sunday.

guide.title: Yesterday and tomorrow are the same word
guide.text:
কাল (kaal) means the day next to today in either direction: tomorrow or yesterday. পরশু (porshu) is two days away: the day after tomorrow or the day before yesterday. The tense of the verb tells you which.

আমি কাল আসব - I will come tomorrow.
আমি কাল এসেছিলাম - I came yesterday.

When it must be unambiguous, use গতকাল (gotokaal) 'yesterday' and আগামীকাল (aagaameekaal) 'tomorrow'.

Other useful words: এখন (ekhon) now; আজ (aaj) today; আজকাল (aajkaal) nowadays; রোজ (roj) every day; দেরি (deri) lateness, delay; তাড়াতাড়ি (taaraataari) quickly, early; পর্যন্ত (porjonto) until.

phrases.note: Add -taa to the number when telling the hour.

phrases.english: It is half past one now.
phrases.note: Not সাড়ে একটা.

phrases.english: Please come at half past seven.
The day after tomorrow is Sunday.
phrases.note: পরশু can also mean the day before yesterday.
'kaal' means both tomorrow and yesterday; the verb tense tells which.
Literally 'stand for a minute'.

phrases.english: Until what time is the shop open?
I don't have time right now.
phrases.note: 'nei' means 'there is not' - the negative of 'aachhe'.

units.title: Weather and seasons
units.description: Talk about heat, rain, cold and storms, say how the weather feels to you, and name the seasons.

guide.title: Weather happens
guide.text:
There is no 'it' in Bengali weather sentences. The weather itself is the subject, and it happens, falls, rises or gives.

বৃষ্টি (brishti) rain: বৃষ্টি হচ্ছে or বৃষ্টি পড়ছে, 'rain is happening / falling'.
রোদ (rod) sunshine: রোদ উঠেছে, 'the sun has come out'.
মেঘ (megh) cloud: মেঘ করেছে, 'it has clouded over'.
হাওয়া (haaowaa) wind: হাওয়া দিচ্ছে, 'the wind is blowing' (in Bangladesh the usual word is বাতাস, baataash).
ঝড় (jhor) storm: ঝড় আসছে, 'a storm is coming'.
কুয়াশা (kuyaashaa) fog: কুয়াশা পড়েছে।

Heat and cold 'fall' too: গরম পড়েছে, 'the hot weather has set in'; ঠান্ডা পড়েছে, 'it has turned cold'.

A plain description needs no verb: আজ খুব গরম, 'it is very hot today'; আকাশ পরিষ্কার, 'the sky is clear'.

guide.title: How it feels to you
guide.text:
To say that YOU feel hot or cold, use লাগা 'to strike, to feel' with yourself in the possessive: আমার গরম লাগছে, 'I feel hot'; আমার ঠান্ডা লাগছে, 'I feel cold'.

Do not say আমি গরম or আমি ঠান্ডা: that describes your temperature to the touch, or your temper.

The same verb gives liking: শীতকাল আমার ভালো লাগে, 'I like winter'.

And with the perfect, catching a cold: আমার ঠান্ডা লেগেছে।

guide.title: Six seasons
guide.text:
The Bengali year traditionally has six seasons of two months each:

গ্রীষ্ম (greeshsho) summer - the hot months before the rains
বর্ষা (borshaa) the monsoon
শরৎ (shorot) early autumn - clear skies, the season of Durga Puja
হেমন্ত (hemonto) late autumn - harvest
শীত (sheet) winter
বসন্ত (boshonto) spring

In everyday talk three matter most, with কাল (kaal) 'season, time' attached: গরমকাল (goromkaal) the hot season, বর্ষাকাল (borshaakaal) the rainy season, শীতকাল (sheetkaal) the cold season.

The Bengali new year, পয়লা বৈশাখ (poylaa boishaakh), falls in mid-April at the start of summer.

examples.english: It rains a lot in the monsoon.

phrases.english: It has turned very hot today.

phrases.note: Equally common: বৃষ্টি হচ্ছে (brishti hochchhe).
In Bangladesh: বাতাস (baataash) for wind.

phrases.english: It rains a lot in the monsoon.
It rained a lot last night.

phrases.note: A familiar sight in Kolkata and Dhaka after heavy rain.

units.title: Health & emergencies
units.description: Get help, describe what hurts or what is wrong, and report something lost or stolen.

guide.title: Calling for help
guide.text:
The cry for help is বাঁচান! (baanchaan), literally 'save (me)!'. A calmer request is আমাকে একটু সাহায্য করুন, 'please help me a little'.

ডাকা (daakaa) is 'to call, to summon': পুলিশ ডাকুন, 'call the police'; ডাক্তার ডাকুন, 'call a doctor'; অ্যাম্বুলেন্স ডাকুন, 'call an ambulance'.

Other words to recognise: বিপদ (bipod) danger; আগুন (aagun) fire; চোর (chor) thief; সাবধান! (shaabdhaan) careful!; তাড়াতাড়ি! (taaraataari) quickly!

সাহায্য is pronounced shaa-haaj-jo: the য-ফলা doubles the j.

guide.title: Saying what is wrong with you
guide.text:
Illness 'happens to' you; you are in the possessive.

আমার জ্বর হয়েছে - I have a fever. (জ্বর is jor: the ব is silent.)
আমার সর্দি হয়েছে (shordi) - I have a cold. কাশি (kaashi) is a cough.
আমার পেট খারাপ হয়েছে - I have an upset stomach.

Pain is ব্যথা (byathaa), and it 'does': the part that hurts + ব্যথা করছে. আমার পেট ব্যথা করছে, 'my stomach is hurting'; মাথা ব্যথা করছে, 'my head aches'. If you cannot name the place, point and say এখানে ব্যথা করছে।

The general complaint is আমার শরীর ভালো নেই, 'my body is not well', or শরীর খারাপ লাগছে, 'I feel unwell'.

Parts of the body: মাথা (maathaa) head; চোখ (chokh) eye; কান (kaan) ear; দাঁত (daant) tooth; গলা (golaa) throat; বুক (buk) chest; পেট (pet) stomach; পিঠ (pith) back; হাত (haat) hand, arm; পা (paa) foot, leg.

guide.title: Doctor, hospital, medicine
guide.text:
ডাক্তার (daaktaar) doctor - addressed as ডাক্তারবাবু (daaktaarbaabu) in West Bengal.
হাসপাতাল (haashpaataal) hospital.
ওষুধ (oshudh) medicine; ওষুধের দোকান (oshudher dokaan) a pharmacy.

'To see a doctor' is ডাক্তার দেখানো, literally 'to show (oneself to) a doctor'.

What you need is said with লাগবে: আমার ওষুধ লাগবে, 'I need medicine'.

Allergies and conditions can be stated simply: আমার ডায়াবেটিস আছে, 'I have diabetes'.

guide.title: Lost and stolen
guide.text:
Things get lost and stolen 'by themselves' in Bengali, with the helper verb যাওয়া:

হারিয়ে গেছে (haariye gechhe) 'has got lost': আমার ফোনটা হারিয়ে গেছে।
চুরি হয়ে গেছে (churi hoye gechhe) 'has got stolen': আমার ব্যাগটা চুরি হয়ে গেছে।

If you want to say that you yourself lost it, use ফেলা: আমি পাসপোর্টটা হারিয়ে ফেলেছি।

আগুন লেগেছে, 'fire has caught', is how you say that something is on fire.

phrases.note: Literally 'save (me)!' - the cry for help in real danger.
অ্যা at the start of a loanword is the a of 'cat'.
Literally 'my body is not well'.
The ব in জ্বর is silent.
Point to the place while saying it.

units.title: Phone and appointments
units.description: Make and answer a phone call, cope with a bad line, and fix a time to meet.

guide.title: On the phone
guide.text:
A call opens with হ্যালো (hyaalo). To ask who is calling: কে বলছেন? 'who is speaking?' To say who you are: আমি রাজ বলছি, 'I Raj am-speaking'. Bengali uses 'I', not 'this is'.

To ask for someone: রাজ আছে? 'Is Raj there?' - or respectfully রাজবাবু আছেন? The answers: হ্যাঁ, ধরুন, 'yes, hold on'; উনি এখন নেই, 'he is not here now'.

The verbs: ফোন করা (phon koraa) to phone; ফোন ধরা (dhoraa) to answer, to hold; ফোন রাখা (raakhaa) to hang up; ফোন কেটে যাওয়া (kete jaaowaa) to get cut off.

রাখছি (raakhchhi), 'I am putting (the phone) down', is the normal way to end a call.

examples.english: He/She is not here right now.

guide.title: When you cannot hear
guide.text:
'I can't hear' is said without 'I': শোনা যাচ্ছে না, 'hearing is not going' - it can't be heard. This is the verbal noun + যাওয়া pattern for what can or cannot be done.

জোরে (jore) is 'loudly' and আস্তে (aaste) is 'softly, slowly': একটু জোরে বলুন, 'speak a little louder'; একটু আস্তে বলুন, 'speak a little slower'.

লাইন (laain) is the line; নেটওয়ার্ক নেই, 'there is no network'.

guide.title: Fixing a time
guide.text:
দেখা করা (dekhaa koraa) is 'to meet (by arrangement)'; দেখা হওয়া is 'to meet (as it happens)', which gives the goodbye দেখা হবে, 'we'll meet'.

To propose: কাল কি আপনার সময় আছে? 'Do you have time tomorrow?'; কাল দশটায় দেখা করতে পারি? 'Can we meet at ten tomorrow?'; কটায়? 'At what time?'; কোথায়? 'Where?'

To agree: ঠিক আছে, 'fine'; তাহলে (taahole) 'then, in that case' rounds it off: তাহলে কাল দেখা হবে।

A doctor or official 'sits' during consulting hours: ডাক্তারবাবু কখন বসবেন? 'When will the doctor be in?'

To send a text: মেসেজ করা or মেসেজ পাঠানো (paathaano).

examples.english: Can we meet at ten tomorrow?

examples.native: ঠিক আছে, তাহলে কাল দেখা হবে।
examples.roman: thik aachhe, taahole kaal dekhaa hobe.
examples.english: All right, see you tomorrow then.

phrases.english: He/She is not here right now.
Can we meet at ten tomorrow?
When will the doctor be in?
phrases.note: A doctor 'sits' at the clinic. West Bengal usage.

phrases.native: ঠিক আছে, তাহলে কাল দেখা হবে।
phrases.roman: thik aachhe, taahole kaal dekhaa hobe.
phrases.english: All right, see you tomorrow then.
phrases.literal: right is, then tomorrow meeting will-be

units.title: Travel and staying somewhere
units.description: Buy tickets, ask about departures and arrivals, find your seat, and take a room in a hotel.

guide.title: Tickets and trains
guide.text:
টিকিট (tikit) ticket. A ticket TO a place uses the possessive: ঢাকার টিকিট, 'Dhaka's ticket'. 'To buy a ticket' is টিকিট কাটা, literally 'to cut a ticket'.

ছাড়া (chhaaraa) to leave, depart: ট্রেনটা কখন ছাড়বে? 'When will the train leave?'
পৌঁছানো (pounchhaano) to arrive, reach: আমরা কখন পৌঁছাব? 'When will we arrive?'
ওঠা (othaa) to get on; নামা (naamaa) to get off.

প্ল্যাটফর্ম (plyaatphorm) platform; সিট (sit) seat; মালপত্র (maalpotro) luggage; পরের স্টেশন (porer steshon) the next station; দেরি (deri) delay: ট্রেন দেরিতে আসছে, 'the train is running late'.

খালি (khaali) means 'empty, free, vacant': a seat, a room, a taxi.

guide.title: Taking a room
guide.text:
ঘর (ghor) is a room (in Bangladesh usually রুম, rum). ঘর খালি আছে? 'Is a room free?'

ভাড়া (bhaaraa) is the charge: এক রাতের ভাড়া কত? 'one night's rent how much?'

To say how long you will stay, use থাকা with the number of days or nights: আমরা দুদিন থাকব, 'we will stay two days'. দুদিন (dudin) is 'two days'; তিন রাত, 'three nights'; এক সপ্তাহ, 'a week'.

Useful things to ask about: গরম জল (gorom jol) hot water; এসি (esi) air conditioning; পাখা (paakhaa) fan; চাবি (chaabi) key; তোয়ালে (toyaale) towel.

এই যে (ei je), 'here it is', is what you say when handing something over or pointing it out: এই যে আমার পাসপোর্ট।

examples.english: Do you have a room free?
How much is it for one night?

guide.title: 'Where shall I ...?' and 'May I ...?'
guide.text:
The first-person future as a question asks for instructions: মালপত্র কোথায় রাখব? 'Where shall I put the luggage?'; কোথায় নামব? 'Where should I get off?'; ট্যাক্সি কোথায় পাব? 'Where will I get a taxi?'

For permission, use the -te form + পারি: ঘরটা একটু দেখতে পারি? 'May I have a look at the room?'

Both are softened, as always, with একটু.

examples.english: Where shall I put the luggage?
Where can I get a taxi?

phrases.english: Which platform will the train come to?
I'll get off at the next station.
Where shall I put the luggage?
Where can I get a taxi?
Do you have a room free?
phrases.note: In Bangladesh: রুম (rum).

phrases.english: How much is it for one night?

phrases.note: In Bangladesh: গরম পানি (gorom paani).
এই যে is said when handing something over.

units.title: At work or study
units.description: Say what you do and where, talk about being busy or free, and ask for explanations in class or at the office.

guide.title: What do you do?
guide.text:
কাজ (kaaj) is work; কাজ করা, to work. চাকরি (chaakri) is a salaried job; চাকরি করা, to be employed. ব্যবসা (byabshaa) is business.

A profession is stated with no verb and no article: আমি শিক্ষক, 'I am a teacher'; উনি ইঞ্জিনিয়ার, 'he/she is an engineer'.

Where you work takes the 'at' ending: আমি একটা ব্যাংকে কাজ করি; আমি অফিসে যাচ্ছি.

Some professions: শিক্ষক (shikkhok) teacher; ডাক্তার doctor; উকিল (ukil) lawyer; ব্যবসায়ী (byabshaayee) businessman; সাংবাদিক (shaangbaadik) journalist; চাষি (chaashi) farmer; ছাত্র / ছাত্রী student.

ছুটি (chhuti) is a holiday, leave, or the end of the working day: আজ আমার ছুটি, 'I am off today'; কটায় ছুটি? 'when do you finish?'

examples.english: I am looking for a job.

guide.title: Reading, studying, teaching
guide.text:
পড়া (poraa) means both 'to read' and 'to study'. আমি কলেজে পড়ি is 'I study at college'; আপনি কী নিয়ে পড়ছেন? is 'what are you studying?' (literally 'taking what are you studying').

Bengali makes 'cause to do' verbs by adding -আনো (-aano) to the stem. These pairs are worth learning together:

পড়া to study - পড়ানো (poraano) to teach
শেখা (shekhaa) to learn - শেখানো (shekhaano) to teach (a skill)
বোঝা (bojhaa) to understand - বোঝানো (bojhaano) to explain
দেখা to see - দেখানো (dekhaano) to show

So: আমি বাংলা শিখছি, 'I am learning Bengali'; উনি বাংলা পড়ান, 'he/she teaches Bengali'; আমাকে বুঝিয়ে দিন, 'explain it to me'.

স্কুল (skul) school; কলেজ (kolej) college; বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় (bisshobiddaaloy) university; ক্লাস (klaas) class; পরীক্ষা (poreekkhaa) exam.

guide.title: When: কখন and কবে
guide.text:
Bengali has two words for 'when'. কখন (kokhon) asks for a time of day: মিটিংটা কখন? 'What time is the meeting?' কবে (kobe) asks for a day or date: পরীক্ষা কবে? 'When (which day) is the exam?'

ব্যস্ত (byasto) is 'busy'; the য-ফলা gives the a of 'cat'. Its opposite is ফাঁকা (phaankaa) 'free, empty' or simply সময় আছে, 'there is time'.

শেষ (shesh) is 'end, finished': শেষ হবে, 'will be finished'; শেষ করব, 'I will finish'. শুরু (shuru) is 'beginning': কখন শুরু হবে? 'when will it begin?'

বানান (baanaan) is 'spelling' and শব্দ (shobdo) is 'word' - two words every learner needs: এই শব্দটার বানান কী?

examples.english: The work will be finished tomorrow.

phrases.note: The য-ফলা in ব্যস্ত gives the a of 'cat'.

phrases.english: The work will be finished tomorrow.
I am looking for a job.

phrases.note: Asks for the subject. নিয়ে here means 'about, on'.
কবে asks which day; কখন asks what time.

units.title: Everyday conversation
units.description: Keep a conversation going: say when you have not understood, react naturally and make small talk.

guide.title: When you do not understand
guide.text:
The most useful sentences for a learner are the ones that slow the other person down.

আমি বুঝতে পারছি না - 'I am not able to understand' (what you are saying now). বুঝিনি, 'I didn't catch that', is shorter.

একটু আস্তে বলুন - 'speak a little slowly'. আস্তে means both slowly and softly.

আর একবার বলুন - 'say it one more time'. একবার (ekbaar) is 'once'; আর is 'more'.

To ask about a word: এর মানে কী? 'what is the meaning of this?'; এটাকে কী বলে? 'what does one call this?'; বাংলায় কী বলে? 'what do you say in Bengali?'

Bengalis are delighted when a foreigner tries their language, and will usually switch to simpler Bengali rather than English if you ask.

guide.title: Little words that keep talk going
guide.text:
আচ্ছা (aachchhaa) okay; I see; well then
তাই? (taai) or তাই নাকি? (taai naaki) is that so? really?
সত্যি? (shotti) really? truly?
ঠিক (thik) right, exactly; ঠিক আছে, okay
হ্যাঁ হ্যাঁ yes, yes (I follow)
মানে (maane) I mean ..., that is ...
কিন্তু (kintu) but
তো (to) a particle with no single translation: it turns a statement into 'surely ...', 'well ...', 'but then ...'
না না no, no - a modest protest

নাকি (naaki) at the end of a sentence means 'is it so, as I hear?': আপনি নাকি চলে যাচ্ছেন? 'I hear you are leaving?'

guide.title: Liking: ভালো লাগা
guide.text:
'To like' is ভালো লাগা (bhaalo laagaa), 'to feel good'. The thing liked is the subject; the person who likes it is in the possessive.

এই জায়গাটা আমার খুব ভালো লাগে - 'this place feels very good to me' - I really like this place.

General liking is in the simple present (লাগে). A reaction right now is continuous (লাগছে): কেমন লাগছে? 'How do you like it (so far)?' A reaction to something just finished is past (লাগল): খুব ভালো লাগল, 'I enjoyed it very much'.

The negative is ভালো লাগে না, 'I don't like', and the opposite খারাপ লাগা, 'to feel bad'.

You can also say পছন্দ (pochhondo) 'liking, choice': এটা আমার পছন্দ, 'I like this one'; আমি এটা পছন্দ করি।

examples.native: এই জায়গাটা আমার খুব ভালো লাগে।
examples.roman: ei jaaygaataa aamaar khub bhaalo laage.

guide.title: Small talk
guide.text:
Conversation with a stranger usually starts with where you are from, what you do, and your family - questions that are friendly in Bengal, not intrusive. Expect to be asked your home town, your job, whether you are married and how many children you have.

Then the weather (আজ খুব গরম), food (খেয়েছেন?), and how long you have been here: আপনি এখানে কতদিন আছেন? - literally 'how many days are you here?', with the present tense where English says 'have you been'.

The great Bengali institution is আড্ডা (aaddaa): long, unhurried talk among friends, over tea. An invitation to it is simply চলুন, চা খাই।

A guest who is leaving is told আবার আসবেন, 'do come again'.

examples.english: How long have you been here?

phrases.note: The negative 'naa' comes after the verb.
'ektu' (a little) softens the request, like 'please'.
Add বাংলায় (baanglaay), 'in Bengali', at the front if you need to.
Shows interest or surprise.

phrases.english: How long have you been here?
phrases.note: Present tense in Bengali.

phrases.native: এই জায়গাটা আমার খুব ভালো লাগে।
phrases.roman: ei jaaygaataa aamaar khub bhaalo laage.
phrases.literal: this place-the my very good feels
phrases.note: 'bhaalo laage' (feels good) is how Bengali says 'like'.
Said to a departing guest.

units.title: Feelings and opinions
units.description: Say how you feel, what you think, and whether you agree - using the 'it happens to me' pattern that Bengali prefers.

guide.title: Feelings happen to you
guide.text:
A few feelings are plain adjectives, used with আমি and no verb: আমি খুশি (khushi) 'I am happy'; আমি ক্লান্ত (klaanto) 'I am tired'; আমি অবাক (obaak) 'I am astonished'.

But most feelings are nouns that 'happen' or 'do' or 'come' to a person, who is put in the possessive. You do not say 'I am afraid' but 'my fear is doing'.

ভয় করা - আমার ভয় করছে (bhoy korchhe) I am scared
রাগ হওয়া - আমার রাগ হচ্ছে (raag hochchhe) I am getting angry
লজ্জা করা - আমার লজ্জা করছে (lojjaa korchhe) I feel shy, embarrassed
ঘুম পাওয়া - আমার ঘুম পাচ্ছে (ghum paachchhe) I am sleepy
কষ্ট হওয়া - আমার কষ্ট হচ্ছে (koshto hochchhe) I am suffering, it is hard for me
আনন্দ হওয়া - আমার খুব আনন্দ হচ্ছে (aanondo hochchhe) I am very glad

মন (mon) is the mind or heart: আমার মন খারাপ, 'my mind is bad' - I am feeling low; মন ভালো নেই, 'I'm not in good spirits'.

guide.title: Good and bad: লাগা
guide.text:
লাগা 'to strike, to feel' is the general verb of reaction. With ভালো it is liking and enjoyment; with খারাপ, dislike and feeling bad.

আমার খুব ভালো লাগছে - I am feeling very good / I am enjoying this.
আমার খুব খারাপ লাগছে - I feel very bad (sorry, upset or unwell).
খুব ভালো লাগল - I enjoyed it very much (said afterwards).
কেমন লাগল? - How did you like it?

'To love' is one word, ভালোবাসা (bhaalobaashaa), and is a normal verb with আমি as subject: আমি তোমাকে ভালোবাসি। It is used for people; for things you love, say খুব ভালো লাগে or খুব ভালোবাসি - both are heard.

guide.title: I think, in my opinion
guide.text:
'I think' is আমার মনে হয় (aamaar mone hoy), 'in my mind it happens'. The thing you think simply follows: আমার মনে হয় বৃষ্টি হবে, 'I think it will rain'. For an impression of the moment: মনে হচ্ছে, 'it seems'.

To ask: আপনার কী মনে হয়? 'What do you think?'

মত (mot) is 'opinion': আমার মতে (aamaar mote) 'in my opinion'; একমত (ekmot) 'of one opinion': আমি আপনার সঙ্গে একমত, 'I agree with you'.

ঠিক (thik) right; ভুল (bhul) wrong, a mistake: আপনি ঠিকই বলছেন, 'you are quite right'; আমার ভুল হয়েছে, 'I made a mistake'.

পছন্দ (pochhondo) 'liking': আমার এটা পছন্দ, 'I like this'; পছন্দ নয়, 'I don't like it'.

To reassure someone: চিন্তা করবেন না, 'don't worry'; কিছু হবে না, 'nothing will happen'.

phrases.note: Also 'I am really enjoying this'.
A sincere way to say you are sorry about something.
Said after a meal, a visit, a film.
Always with তুমি: love is not formal.

units.title: Joining sentences
units.description: Link ideas with and, or, but, so, because, if, when and that, and with the -e and -le forms of the verb.

guide.title: And, also, or, but
guide.text:
আর (aar) is the everyday 'and'; it also means 'more, else'. এবং (ebong) is the written, formal 'and'.

ও (o) is 'too, also, even'. It is attached to the END of the word it applies to: আমিও, 'I too'; এটাও, 'this one as well'. Between two nouns it can mean 'and': মা ও বাবা।

বা (baa) and অথবা (othobaa) are 'or' in statements. In a question offering a choice, 'or' is না (naa): চা না কফি? 'tea or coffee?'

কিন্তু (kintu) is 'but'. তবে (tobe) is a softer 'but, though, however'.

examples.english: I will have tea and biscuits.
I'd like to, but I have no time.

guide.title: So and because
guide.text:
তাই (taai) is 'so, therefore': বৃষ্টি হচ্ছে, তাই যাইনি - 'it's raining, so I haven't gone'.

কারণ (kaaron) is 'because' and comes, as in English, before the reason: আমি যাব না, কারণ আমার জ্বর।

The most natural spoken way puts the reason FIRST, followed by বলে (bole, literally 'having said'): আমার জ্বর বলে আমি যাব না - 'I have a fever, saying which, I won't go'.

জন্য (jonno) after a possessive also gives a reason: বৃষ্টির জন্য, 'because of the rain'; সেই জন্য or সেজন্য, 'for that reason'.

examples.english: It's raining, so I haven't gone.

examples.native: আমি যাব না, কারণ আমার জ্বর।
examples.roman: aami jaabo naa, kaaron aamaar jor.
examples.english: I won't go because I have a fever.

examples.native: আমার জ্বর বলে আমি যাব না।
examples.roman: aamaar jor bole aami jaabo naa.
examples.english: I won't go, as I have a fever.

guide.title: If and when: the -le form
guide.text:
The compact way to say 'if' or 'when' is a verb form ending in -লে (-le), made on the same stem as the simple past. It does not change for person.

করা - করলে (korle) if/when (someone) does
হওয়া - হলে (hole); যাওয়া - গেলে (gele); আসা - এলে (ele); খাওয়া - খেলে (khele); দেওয়া - দিলে (dile); পাওয়া - পেলে (pele)

বৃষ্টি হলে আমি যাব না - 'rain if-happens, I won't go'.
আপনি এলে আমরা খাব - 'you when-come, we will eat'.

The negative puts না BEFORE the verb: না হলে (naa hole) 'if not, otherwise'; আপনি না এলে, 'if you don't come'.

The fuller pattern uses the pair যদি (jodi) 'if' ... তাহলে (taahole) or তবে 'then', with ordinary tenses: যদি পারেন, তাহলে আসবেন।

তাহলে on its own is the conversational 'then, in that case'.

examples.english: If it rains, I won't go.
When you come, we will eat.

guide.title: Pairs: when ... then, what ... that
guide.text:
Bengali likes to build longer sentences in matched pairs: a word beginning with য- (j-) opens the first half, and its partner beginning with ত- or স- answers it in the second.

যখন (jokhon) when ... তখন (tokhon) then
যা (jaa) what ... তা (taa) or তাই (taai) that
যে (je) who, the one who ... সে (she) he/she
যেখানে (jekhaane) where ... সেখানে (shekhaane) there
যত (joto) as much ... তত (toto) so much

যখন সময় পাব, তখন করব - 'when I get time, then I'll do it'.
আপনি যা বলবেন, তাই হবে - 'what you say, just that will be'.

যে is also the plain 'that' after verbs of knowing and saying: আমি জানি যে সে আসবে, 'I know that he will come'. It is often left out.

examples.english: I'll do it when I get time.
It will be just as you say.
I know that he/she will come.

guide.title: Doing one thing after another
guide.text:
Two actions by the same person are joined not with 'and' but by putting the first verb in the -e form ('having done'): খেয়ে আসুন, 'having eaten, come'; বাড়ি গিয়ে ফোন করব, 'having gone home, I'll phone' - I'll phone when I get home.

'Before' and 'after' follow the verbal noun in the possessive: খাওয়ার পরে (khaaowaar pore) 'after eating'; যাওয়ার আগে (jaaowaar aage) 'before going'.

'While doing' is the -te form said twice: যেতে যেতে (jete jete) 'while going, on the way'; খেতে খেতে, 'while eating'.

examples.english: I'll phone when I get home.

units.title: Dialogue: meeting someone on a train
units.description: Follow and take part in a complete polite conversation with a stranger, from the first question to the goodbye.

guide.title: The situation
guide.text:
You get into a train at Howrah and start talking to the passenger beside you. The phrases of this unit are the lines of the conversation in order; read them from top to bottom as a script. The two speakers do not strictly alternate (the other passenger sometimes says two lines in a row) - the notes say who is speaking.

Both speakers are adults who have never met, so everything is in the polite আপনি form: যাচ্ছেন, বলেন, শিখলেন, খাবেন. Listen for the -en ending throughout.

The conversation follows the usual course of Bengali small talk: where are you going, how do you know Bengali, how do you like it here - and then tea.

guide.title: Things to notice
guide.text:
তো (to) appears twice. In আপনি তো বেশ ভালো বাংলা বলেন it expresses pleasant surprise: 'why, you speak Bengali quite well!' In দুটো চা দিন তো it makes a request casual and friendly: 'two teas here, will you'.

না না - the modest double 'no' with which a compliment is turned aside.

একটু একটু পারি - 'I can (manage) a little'. পারা used alone means 'to be able to cope with, to know how'.

কেমন লাগছে? - 'how is it feeling?' - asks for your impression so far, so it is continuous. The answer keeps the same verb: খুব ভালো লাগছে।

গরমটা একটু বেশি - 'the heat is a bit much'. -টা on গরম makes it 'the heat (here)'.

খেতে পারি - 'I could have some': a polite, unhurried yes.

আমারও - 'mine too': the reply to ভালো লাগল, because the full sentence would be আমারও ভালো লাগল।

units.title: Dialogue: buying mangoes
units.description: Follow and take part in a complete bargaining conversation at a fruit stall, with prices, quantities and change.

guide.title: The situation
guide.text:
You are at a fruit stall in a Kolkata market in May, when the mangoes come in. The phrases of this unit are the lines of the conversation in order; the notes say who is speaking.

Customer and stallholder call each other আপনি, and you address him as দাদা. The tone is brisk and good-humoured: bargaining is a game both sides enjoy, and nobody is offended by a low offer.

The arithmetic: he asks 100 a kilo, you offer 80, you settle on 90; two kilos come to 180; you pay with 200 and get 20 back.

guide.title: Things to notice
guide.text:
আমের দাম - 'the price of mangoes': আম + the possessive -এর.

একশো টাকা কিলো - 'a hundred rupees a kilo'. No word for 'per' is needed.

খেয়ে দেখুন - 'eat and see': the -e form + দেখা means 'try doing'. In the same way পরে দেখুন, 'try it on'; বলে দেখুন, 'try asking'.

না হলে - 'if it is not (so)': the -le form of হওয়া with না before it. ফেরত দেবেন, 'you will give back'.

আশি টাকায় - 'for eighty rupees': the price you buy AT takes the 'at' ending. আশিতে হবে না - 'at eighty it won't do'.

হবে না is the all-purpose refusal: 'no can do'.

এই থাক - 'let this stay', that is, 'that will be all'. থাক is the 'let it' form of থাকা.

এই নিন - 'here, take': said when handing something over.

units.title: Dialogue: two friends make a plan
units.description: Follow and take part in a complete informal conversation between friends, using the familiar 'tumi' forms throughout.

guide.title: The situation
guide.text:
Two friends who have not met for a long time run into each other in the street and arrange to see a film. The phrases of this unit are the lines of the conversation in order; the two speakers simply alternate, starting with the first friend.

Everything here is in the familiar তুমি form. Compare the endings with the polite ones you know:

আপনি কেমন আছেন? - তুমি কেমন আছ?
আপনি কোথায় থাকেন? - তুমি কোথায় থাকো?
আপনি কী করছেন? - তুমি কী করছ?
চলুন - চলো
দেরি করবেন না - দেরি কোরো না

And the possessive: আপনার খবর - তোমার খবর।

guide.title: Things to notice
guide.text:
আরে (aare) is an exclamation of surprise, 'hey!', 'oh!'.

এই চলছে - 'it's going on like this': the standard modest answer to 'how are things?'

দেখা হয়নি - 'meeting has not happened': the -নি negative of দেখা হয়েছে.

বাড়িতেই - the particle -ই adds 'the very, the same, only': পুরোনো বাড়িতেই, 'in that same old house'. এখনো is 'still'.

চলো, ... দেখি - 'come on, let's watch': চলো + a first-person present verb.

কটায়? ছটায়। - 'at what time? at six.' The 'at' ending on the clock words.

টিকিট কেটে রাখব - 'I'll buy the tickets and keep them': the helper রাখা means doing something in advance.

দেরি কোরো না কিন্তু - কিন্তু ('but') tacked on at the end of a command means 'mind you'.

ঠিক সময়ে - 'at the right time', on time.
